### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 39 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dcc13b856b81fa17f3a13aca6688d43487ba8638` — the merge of head `0027ae7fe025bb571c13d9a6c25b4e0bf1aeaff0` into base `725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dcc13b856b81fa17f3a13aca6688d43487ba8638 && git checkout dcc13b856b81fa17f3a13aca6688d43487ba8638
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8 0027ae7fe025bb571c13d9a6c25b4e0bf1aeaff0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8 && git merge --no-ff 0027ae7fe025bb571c13d9a6c25b4e0bf1aeaff0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 725a5b1311ecc051edafcd8122ad47dfe1ccfbf8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

| Serial | Open PR file lists read in this act. Only PR #24451 (#24340, `domain:services`) touches `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, in `defaultRowScope`'s docblock (about `:2973`). This PR edits `ObjectExtensionSchema`'s `guidance.actions` (about `:3983`). The hunks are disjoint, so whichever lands second merges. | Accepted deviations | (a) `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` instead of the claim's `yes (widening)`: dispatch G4 named this spelling for a diff that widens and narrows. (b) `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`, outside the claim's file surface: a one-row hand-written mirror of the re-trued sentence. Leaving it would keep the false promise in the docs. (c) G1 measured false: `defineStack` refused a foreign target in any stack with objects, so the spec half is a scoped widening, not documentation only. |
| Open question 1 (which foreign targets `defineStack` accepts) | **Seat answer: A, as implemented.** It is the narrowest acceptance that makes the guidance's own route real (the guidance is written for an extension body), plus the named platform list #24318 needs. A typo still fails at build. B moves every typo to boot, and C reopens `artifactObjects`' recorded scope. Not escalated: it executes the premise-bound ruling (implement the promised route), and no product semantics split. |
| Open question 2 (a name collision) | **Seat answer: A for this PR.** The object's own declaration wins, by the router's rung-1 precedence. Refusing a collision (B) is a narrowing that the ruling never named, and it needs a declaration-sameness measurement first. B would also hard-fail #24318's transition boot. The contract review is asked to judge this against the card's "never silently dropped". |
| Findings | Two class-b findings, measured at the public door (`defineStack`): the same guidance tells an author to declare a top-level `hook` or `view` bound to the target, and both are refused at build. One card for the family is filed at adoption. Two items are noted, not filed: the handler-key collision in `ObjectQL.actions` (read in code, no booted reach), and the stored-overlay staleness. Both are in the PR's Acceptance notes. |
| Landing | After a contract-review PASS and a green head: `pr_ready` then `automerge_enable`. `Fixes #24400` closes the card. |

Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/action-governance.ts (read, unchanged), packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts (read, unchanged), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (read, unchanged), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (read, unchanged), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (read, unchanged), packages/metadata-core/src/code-artifact-provenance.ts (read, unchanged), packages/core/src/kernel.ts and lite-kernel.ts (read, unchanged), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (read, unchanged), packages/objectql/src/bound-action-foreign-object.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-bound-action-foreign-object.test.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx, .changeset/24400-bound-action-foreign-object.md

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The served widening lands at the one tail — right.** `finishServedObject` (registry.ts :3472) is the last line of `foldExtendersOntoDefinition` (:3459). Three callers reach it and nothing reads an object around it: `resolveObject` (:3379, through `foldExtenders`), the code layer `resolveOwnerLayer` (:4364, through `foldExtenders`), and `foldObjectExtendersOnto` on all three of its branches (:3704 no fqn, :3706 no extender, and the fold). The protocol's `readMetaItem` runs step 1 (stored row, protocol.ts :11588) and step 2 (MetadataService copy, :11640) through `foldObjectExtendersFromRegistry` (:9333 to `foldObjectExtendersOnto`); step 3 is `registry.getItem('object')` to `getObject` to `resolveObject`. `engine.getSchema()` is `registry.getObject` (engine.ts :11208); the router's object lookup is `ql.getSchema(objectName) ?? registry.getObject` (action-execution.ts :2961); `getAllObjects` resolves each fqn through `resolveObject` (:4449). MCP `describe_object` serves no `actions`. Nothing sees it twice: `attachBoundActions` builds `present` from the body's own names first, so the same-stack merged copy, a MetadataService copy already carrying it, and a stored overlay written back from a served read each absorb the attach (pinned: same-stack once).

**2. Order independence and cache correctness — right.** The attach is read-time, and every event that changes the answer drops the fold: `registerItem('action')` invalidates the target object (:5092, `invalidate` takes a bare name, :6413); `unregisterItem('action')` and `unregisterItemsByPackage` with any `action/` removal call `invalidateAll` (:5126, :5289); `enablePackage` and `disablePackage` call `invalidateAll` (:5998, :6016); re-registering the target deletes its fqn (`registerObject`, `mergedObjectCache.delete`). `boundCodeActions` leaves out a disabled package's items (`isPackageDisabled`, :5639). No stale path on the registry. Pinned: both registration orders, disable then enable, uninstall. Two copies outside the registry are stale by the pre-existing class the dev's acceptance notes name (the boot-bridged MetadataService copy, a stored overlay round-tripped from a served read): both re-attach on read, but a withdrawn action persists in the copy. See ③.

**3. Cost — in proportion on the stock tree, not indexed.** `boundCodeActions()` walks the whole `action` collection on every attach. In the registry that is once per object per cache fill; through `foldObjectExtendersOnto` (uncached) every protocol read of a stored row or MetadataService copy pays one scan of all standalone actions, and a cold `getAllObjects()` pays objects times actions. A per-objectName index is a cheap follow-up, not a defect here.

**4. P3, who may run it — right, nothing loosened.** The attached entry is the registry item by reference (`fresh.push(action)`; pinned `toBe(registry.getItem('action', name))`), so the router's rung 1 (`obj.actions.find`) now returns the very declaration rung 2 (`registry.getItem('action')` under `ownsRoute`) returned before, carrying its own `requiredPermissions`, `requiresMembershipReach` and execution identity. Only `actions` is rewritten (`{ ...body, actions }`): `managedBy`, object-level write policy and fields are untouched. The handler map (`registerAction`, key `OBJECT:ACTION`, engine.ts :5523) is untouched. Write-through: the served object is a fresh object with a fresh array; its entries are shared exactly as every cached fold's entries already are on every registry read, so no new mutation class is introduced, and a grep of rest, runtime and metadata-protocol found no in-place write to an action entry. One visible wire difference: the attached entry carries the registry's `_packageId` stamp (pinned) while the object's own entries do not; downstream suites are green.

**5. The build-time widening in `defineStack` — right, and only the one arm.** `extendedObjectNames` is read off `objectExtensions[].extend` (:4056); `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` is `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES.has(name)`, the union of `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` and `CLOUD_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` (platform-object-names.ts :160, :197), a named set and not `hasPlatformObjectPrefix`; pinned by the `sys_organizaton` control. The embedded-action arm, the hooks arm (:3822), the views arm (:3846) and the nav arm still judge against `objectNames` alone; `artifactObjects` scope is untouched. `validateCrossReferences` has one caller (:4941), so `composeStacks` moves only through `defineStack`. `strict: false` returns before validation and `mergeActionsIntoObjects` is unchanged. Edge, by design: the named list includes cloud-only objects (`sys_app`, `sys_environment` and the rest), so on an OSS runtime such a binding passes the build and fails the boot by the new rule, loudly.

**6. The boot narrowing — right, judged after every package registered.** The `kernel:ready` hook is registered in `start()` (plugin.ts :857, hook at :906); `ObjectKernel` fires it in phase 3 after every plugin's `start()` (kernel.ts :607) and `LiteKernel` through `triggerHookOrThrow` (:140), so the throw fails both boots (pinned, `INVALID_METADATA` 422 with the message). `findUnboundActionTargets` reads `resolveObjectKey`, the read path's own name resolution. A target from a later package in the same boot is not refused (pinned). Post-boot, the `manifest` door judges after the picklist seal and before the `registerApp` loop and `registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects` (:761 to :772); `declared` holds the residual's objects, every ordered manifest's objects in both authored spellings, and nested `plugins[]`; a refused install registers nothing (pinned: `getItem('action')` is undefined after the refusal). Not judged: a direct post-boot `ql.registerApp` by a plugin (its action attaches on read once the object appears) and tenant-authored `action` rows from `resyncAuthoredActions` (deliberately outside the population, `isCodeArtifactBody`).
Blast radius, read on this head: every top-level `objectName` binding in `examples/**` is same-stack (app-crm `crm_convert_lead` to `crm_lead`; showcase to `showcase_task`, `showcase_invoice`, `showcase_field_zoo`); app-multi-package declares no top-level actions; no plugin, service, cloud-connection or platform-objects package declares a top-level `defineAction` (sys_organization's eight are embedded on the object); scaffolding templates carry none. No shipped composition fails its boot; the dev's booted stock showcase and CRM controls agree.
One order-sensitive seam, by precedent: `marketplace-install-local-plugin` registers its `kernel:ready` hook in `start()` after ObjectQL's, so the ledger rehydrates through the sealed door one artifact at a time in ledger order; a marketplace package binding to an object another marketplace package owns depends on that order. The picklist seal at the same door has the identical shape, so this is the existing class, not a new one.

**7. The name collision — an acceptable deferral, on condition it is filed.** `attachBoundActions` skips a name the object already carries and logs nothing. What runs in that case is unchanged by this PR: rung 1 returns the object's own declaration and its gate, exactly as before (rung 2 was never reached for a name the object declared), and the handler is whichever `registerAction` wrote `OBJECT:ACTION` last (a bare `Map.set`, engine.ts :5523, no diagnostic), pre-existing. The shadowed listing is the listing face of that pre-existing handler-face collision. The card's "never silently dropped" is breached only for a same-name pair, which the card's own evidence does not contain, and a hard refusal would break #24318's transition (the platform object still declaring `change_slug` while the composition adds it). Accepted as a deferral because the seat carries the card; see ③.

The one case the sentence does not state is item 7's same-name shadow. The docs row mirrors the sentence in substance. Out of scope here; the seat files both.

Unpinned and judged by reading: the nested `plugins[]` branch of the two manifest collectors, the residual-object branch of the late door, and the stored-row and MetadataService layers of the protocol read (the harness has neither, so the served-read pin exercises step 3 only). The dev's ablation counts (8 of 14, 1 of 14, 1 of 6) agree with this pin map.

The changeset declares `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/objectql` minor, a `feat(spec,objectql)!:` title, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, one marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` closed on facts, and FROM, TO and Fix lines. Each is what the diff publishes:
